  • had nearly finished (phrase): This is the correct past perfect tense, showing that the program almost finished before the action of turning on the television.

  • had (auxiliary verb (past perfect)): 'Had' is used to form the past perfect tense, but the sentence requires a negative form ('had not' or 'hadn't') to match the meaning.
  • hadn’t (auxiliary verb (past perfect, negative)): This is the contraction of 'had not', which is used to form the negative past perfect tense. The correct structure is 'hadn't been out long', meaning we had not been out for a long time when it started to rain.
